title: Ceasefire 'Holding' — Unless You Live in Beirut
narrative: Israeli and Lebanese officials, with US and French mediation, announced a ceasefire approximately one month ago. The public narrative: the ceasefire is holding, and minor violations have been addressed through diplomatic channels. Israel has insisted it will respond to any provocation but maintains the overall ceasefire remains intact. On May 28, Israel struck the Lebanese capital of Beirut — a city that had been largely spared until that moment.
telemetry: May 28, 13:21 GMT: 'Israel hits Lebanese capital in targeted strike' — Beirut largely spared until now
Israel has ordered Lebanese residents to leave 17% of the country's territory
Israel struck 100 Hezbollah infrastructure sites and fighters in Lebanon (May 27 report)
PM Netanyahu: Israel would 'crush' Hezbollah — public statement, not denied
Evacuation orders covering 17% of national territory contradict 'minor violations' framing
Beirut strike + 100 infrastructure sites + evacuation of 17% of country = de facto military campaign, not ceasefire
analysis: The language of 'targeted strike' and 'ceasefire holding' cannot coexist with the mathematics of 17% of Lebanese territory under evacuation order and 100 infrastructure sites struck. This is not a matter of interpretation. It is a matter of scale. When you order the population of nearly one-fifth of a country to leave their homes, you are not engaged in 'minor violations addressed through diplomatic channels.' You are running a military campaign while calling it something else. The strike on Beirut is significant not because it is the first strike — it is not — but because Beirut had been the one place the diplomatic fiction could point to as evidence the ceasefire was real. Now even that marker is gone. Netanyahu's 'crush' language is public and unretracted. It does not describe a ceasefire participant. It describes a combatant planning escalation.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: You cannot call it a 'ceasefire' while ordering 17% of a country to evacuate, striking its capital, and publicly committing to 'crush' your adversary. That is not a ceasefire. That is a campaign with a press release.
